web_evidence.title: Nine Perfect Strangers
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained chapter-one excerpt externally narrates Yao and Masha, repeatedly naming them as he and she while accessing Yao's perceptions and memories.

web_evidence.title: Liane Moriarty Writing Styles in Nine Perfect Strangers
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly states that the novel is written in third person from the viewpoints of its main characters.

web_evidence.title: Review: Nine Perfect Strangers by Lianne Moriarty
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly identifies third-person narration and describes chapters switching among Frances and the other characters' viewpoints.

web_evidence.title: What's Tracy Curtis Reading?

person_note: The Goodreads passages repeatedly show an external narrator moving among Frances, Heather, Carmel, Jessica, Lars, Zoe, Yao, and other characters while accessing their thoughts, memories, and perceptions. The authorized opening independently demonstrates the same third-person technique, and several opened whole-book sources explicitly describe third-person narration with shifting character viewpoints. First-person forms in the sample occur in dialogue, tagged thought, epigraphs, or illustrative embedded language; generic 'you' occurs in aphorisms, speech, and free-indirect generalizations rather than sustained second-person narration. The viewpoint shifts therefore remain within third person and do not warrant ALTERNATING. No material contrary evidence remains.
